headline: High: Dify’s broad write/network/tooling can cascade into unsafe actions and compliance exposure when paired with Argo Workflows’ API-driven orchestration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can consume API/GRPC-driven workflow inputs, and Dify can wire tools into agent/workflow apps with uploaded knowledge-base files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Dify output is fed into Argo without sanitization. No direct shared channel is documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into Argo workflow parameters without validation
IF Argo templates parse user-controlled fields as executable instructions
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for workflow parameters
Strip instruction-like text from Dify outputs before handoff
Require human review for any generated workflow spec
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Dify touches knowledge-base content, conversation logs, and model-provider/tool credentials. If they share a workspace or Dify uploads content into external model providers, sensitive material can flow across the pair. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or artifact store
IF Dify forwards knowledge-base content or logs to third-party model providers
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Disable sharing of conversation logs into downstream tools
Redact secrets before any cross-agent transfer
Restrict Dify connectors to approved destinations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has allowlisted network egress and API surfaces; Dify has broad network egress, shell, subprocess, and filesystem write. If both operate on the same mutable directory or shared datastore, concurrent writes and side effects can collide. Because Dify explicitly supports shared state via a server datastore, the overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF Argo and Dify are run under the same filesystem permissions without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Turn on external locking around shared resources
Make one agent read-only for shared paths
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is designed for agent/workflow apps and tool wiring, so its outputs can become downstream inputs. Argo then executes workflows via API/GRPC, meaning a mistaken or hallucinated Dify result can trigger real actions if trusted. This is a direct cascade path; I choose high because the blast radius can include irreversible workflow execution.
conditions: IF Argo consumes Dify-generated parameters without verification
IF Dify is allowed to emit workflow specs or action commands
mitigations: Insert a verification step before execution
Require signed or schema-validated outputs
Limit Argo to dry-run mode for generated plans
Add approval gates for destructive workflow steps

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles model-provider API keys, tool credentials, and conversation logs, while Argo processes artifacts and parameters. If regulated data is placed into Dify and then propagated into Argo artifacts or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF Argo artifacts retain the same regulated data class beyond policy limits
mitigations: Classify data before ingestion
Set explicit retention limits in both systems
Block regulated data from conversation logs
Document residency and deletion workflows
